name: Pauci-immune Glomerulonephritis with Anti-Neutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibodies (ANCA)

ethnicAssociations: Less common in Asian and African populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Chapel Hill Consensus Conference Criteria for ANCA-associated Vasculitis

criteria.description: Presence of circulating anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), typically MPO-ANCA or PR3-ANCA
Renal biopsy showing pauci-immune necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis with little or no immune complex deposition
Clinical evidence of rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis with hematuria and proteinuria
Exclusion of other causes of glomerulonephritis such as lupus nephritis or anti-GBM disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ANCA positivity plus renal biopsy demonstrating pauci-immune necrotizing glomerulonephritis with compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of serologic, histopathologic, and clinical data

pathognomonic.notes: Characterized by rapid loss of renal function over days to weeks

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hematuria with dysmorphic red blood cells
searchTerms: blood in urine with abnormal red cells
dysmorphic red blood cells in urine

common.notes: Variable degree of protein loss in urine
searchTerms: proteinuria ranging from mild to severe

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms including malaise and low-grade fever
searchTerms: general feeling of illness with mild fever

common.notes: Elevated blood pressure due to renal dysfunction
searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney problems
blood pressure increase due to kidney issues

common.symptomName: Elevated serum creatinine indicating renal insufficiency
searchTerms: reduced kidney function indicated by creatinine

common.symptomName: Microscopic red blood cell casts in urine sediment
searchTerms: red blood cell fragments in urine

occasional.notes: May occur in systemic ANCA-associated vasculitis
Joint involvement common in systemic vasculitis
Upper respiratory tract involvement in systemic disease

rare.symptomName: Cardiac involvement including pericarditis or myocarditis
Ocular inflammation such as scleritis or episcleritis
Gastrointestinal vasculitis causing abdominal pain or bleeding
searchTerms: abdominal pain from blood vessel inflammation
gut bleeding due to vessel inflammation
intestinal blood vessel inflammation causing pain

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
Urinalysis showing hematuria, proteinuria, and red blood cell casts
imaging: Chest X-ray or CT showing pulmonary infiltrates or hemorrhage in systemic cases
Renal ultrasound typically normal or showing increased echogenicity
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible HLA associations in some populations
other: Renal biopsy demonstrating pauci-immune necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis

distinguishingFeatures: Linear immunofluorescence staining on renal biopsy
Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis without ANCA positivity
Immune complex deposition on renal biopsy
Presence of immune deposits on immunofluorescence
Different serologic markers depending on etiology

redFlags: Rapid decline in renal function over days to weeks
Severe hypertension with signs of hypertensive emergency
New onset of peripheral neuropathy or mononeuritis multiplex
Unexplained systemic constitutional symptoms with renal impairment
references: Jennette JC, Falk RJ, Bacon PA, et al. 2012 Revised International Chapel Hill Consensus Conference Nomenclature of Vasculitides. Arthritis Rheum. 2013 Jan;65(1):1-11.

Kitching AR, Anders HJ, Basu N, et al. ANCA-associated vasculitis. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2020 Feb 6;6(1):71.
